cricket_justification: 100+ pressure balls faced represents roughly 7-10 high-pressure match appearances or 2 seasons of death batting. Statistically robust sample.
50-99 balls faced matches the Empirical Bayes K_bat threshold (50 balls). Performance weight equal to population prior.
example_player: Mujeeb Ur Rahman as batter (64 balls faced, W_conf=0.85)

cricket_justification: 20-49 balls faced represents 2-3 brief pressure cameos. Significant uncertainty remains; score dampened by 40%.
example_player: Mohammed Shami as batter (46 balls faced, W_conf=0.60)

cricket_justification: <20 balls faced is insufficient to draw reliable conclusions. Dampened by 70%, locking player into Tier 4.

75+ legal balls bowled represents 12.5+ pressure overs (typically 6-10 matches of death/collapse bowling). Bowlers face far lower ball volume than batters; 75 balls is the statistical equivalent of 120 batting balls.
example_player: Mujeeb Ur Rahman (107 legal balls, W_conf=1.0) & Bumrah (220 legal balls, W_conf=1.0)

cricket_justification: 36-74 legal balls matches the Empirical Bayes K_bowl threshold (36 balls / 6 overs). 50/50 shrinkage weighting.
18-35 legal balls represents 3-5 overs of pressure bowling. High sample variance; dampened by 40%.
<18 legal balls (<3 overs) is anecdotal. Dampened by 70%, locking player into Tier 4.
example_player: Tristan Stubbs as bowler (6 legal balls, W_conf=0.30)
